Guildford's population increased by around 6,500 between the last two censuses (held in 2011 and 2021). This semi-automated article highlights some of the most notable changes among the local population.

The population passed 140,000

Between the last two censuses (held in 2011 and 2021), the population of Guildford increased by 4.7%, from around 137,200 in 2011 to around 143,600 in 2021.

The population here increased by a smaller percentage than the overall population of the South East (7.5%), and by a smaller percentage than the overall population of England (up 6.6% since the 2011 Census).

In 2021, Guildford was home to around 3.8 people per football pitch-sized piece of land, compared with 3.6 in 2011. This area was among the lowest 45% for population density across English local authority areas at the last census.

This article generally uses percentages to enable comparisons over time and between areas. The percentage point change is also used to show the difference between the 2011 and 2021 percentages.

Population growth was lower in Guildford than across the South East

Median age in Guildford

Between the last two censuses, the average (median) age of Guildford increased by one year, from 38 to 39 years of age.

This area had a lower average (median) age than the South East as a whole in 2021 (41 years) and a slightly lower average (median) age than England (40 years).

The median age is the age of the person in the middle of the group, meaning that one half of the group is younger than that person and the other half is older.

The number of people aged 50 to 64 years rose by around 2,800 (an increase of 11.5%), while the number of residents between 35 and 49 years fell by around 2,200 (7.4% decrease).

The share of residents aged between 50 and 64 years increased by 1.2 percentage points between 2011 and 2021

Rise in private renting

Of Guildford households, 19.6% rented privately in 2021, up from 15.8% in 2011.

In 2021, just over one in eight households (12.7%) lived in socially rented housing, compared with 12.8% in 2011. The percentage of Guildford households that owned their home (outright or with a mortgage or loan) decreased from 68.8% to 66.3%.

The increase in the percentage of privately-rented homes was greater in Guildford (3.8 percentage points) than across the South East (2.9 percentage points, from 16.3% to 19.2%). Across England, the percentage increased by 3.6 percentage points, from 16.8% to 20.5%.

Private renting in Guildford increased by 3.8 percentage points

Unpaid care in Guildford

In 2021, 4.7% of Guildford residents (aged five years and over) reported providing up to 19 hours of unpaid care each week. This figure decreased from 7.6% in 2011. These are age-standardised proportions.

Age-standardised proportions are used throughout this section. They enable comparisons between populations over time and across geographies, as they account for differences in the population size and age structure.

In 2021, 1.2% of residents (aged five years and over) reported providing between 20 and 49 hours of unpaid care each week, compared with 1.0% in 2011. The proportion of Guildford residents (aged five years and over) that provided at least 50 hours of weekly unpaid care increased from 1.8% to 2.1%.

The decrease in the proportion of people (aged five years and over) providing up to 19 hours of weekly unpaid care in Guildford (2.9 percentage points) was similar to the decrease across the South East (2.8 percentage points, from 7.3% to 4.5%). Across England, the proportion fell by 2.8 percentage points, from 7.2% to 4.4%.

Census 2021 was undertaken during the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic. This may have influenced how people perceived and managed their provision of unpaid care, and therefore may have affected how people chose to respond.

Caution should be taken when making comparisons between 2011 and 2021 because of changes in question wording and response options.

The percentage of people (aged five years and over) providing up to 19 hours of weekly unpaid care in Guildford decreased by 2.9 percentage points

Religion in Guildford

In 2021, 39.7% of Guildford residents reported having "No religion", up from 27.8% in 2011. The rise of 11.9 percentage points was the largest increase of all broad religious groups in Guildford. Because the census question about religious affiliation is voluntary and has varying response rates, caution is needed when comparing figures between different areas or between censuses.

Across the South East, the percentage of residents who described themselves as having "No religion" increased from 27.7% to 40.2%, while across England the percentage increased from 24.8% to 36.7%.

In 2021, 48.2% of people in Guildford described themselves as Christian (down from 60.2%), while 7.0% did not state their religion (down from 7.7% the decade before).

There are many factors that can cause changes to the religious profile of an area, such as a changing age structure or residents relocating for work or education. Changes may also be caused by differences in the way individuals chose to self-identify between censuses. Religious affiliation is the religion with which someone connects or identifies, rather than their beliefs or religious practice.

In 2021, 39.7% of usual residents in Guildford reported having "No religion"

Change in employment

The decrease in the percentage of people aged 16 years and over (excluding full-time students) who were employed was greater in Guildford (3.1 percentage points) than across England (0.8 percentage points).

In Guildford, the percentage of people aged 16 years and over who were employed (excluding full-time students) decreased from 59.0% in 2011 to 55.8% in 2021. During the same period, the percentage across England decreased from 56.5% to 55.7%.

The percentage of people aged 16 years and over who were unemployed (excluding full-time students) in Guildford fell from 2.5% to 2.1%, while the percentage of people aged 16 years and over who were retired (economically inactive) increased from 18.9% to 19.4%.

Census 2021 took place during the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic, a period of rapid and unparalleled change; the national lockdown, associated guidance and furlough measures will have affected the labour market and our ability to measure it.

The percentage of people aged 16 years and over who were employed (excluding full-time students) in Guildford decreased by 3.1 percentage points

Change in work hours

In 2021, 12.2% of Guildford residents aged 16 years and over and in employment said they worked 15 hours or less per week. This figure increased from 11.9% in 2011.

In 2021, just under one in seven people (14.1%) said they worked over 49 hours per week, compared with 16.5% in 2011. The percentage of adults in employment working 31 to 48 hours per week increased from 55.0% to 57.0%.

The increase in the percentage of people aged 16 years and over and in employment who said they usually worked 15 hours or less per week in Guildford (0.3 percentage points) was similar to the increase across the South East (0.5 percentage points, from 10.4% to 11.0%). Across England, the percentage increased by 0.6 percentage points, from 9.7% to 10.3%.

Working hours may have been affected by the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic.

The percentage of adults who worked 15 hours or less in Guildford increased by 0.3 percentage points

Guildford residents' country of birth

In the latest census, around 111,700 Guildford residents said they were born in England. This represented 77.8% of the local population. The figure has risen from around 111,100 in 2011, which at the time represented 81.0% of Guildford's population.

Scotland was the next most represented, with around 2,200 Guildford residents reporting this country of birth (1.5%). This figure was down from around 2,400 in 2011, which at the time represented 1.8% of the population of Guildford.

The number of Guildford residents born in South Africa rose from around 1,300 in 2011 (1.0% of the local population) to around 2,000 in 2021 (1.4%).

In 2021, 77.8% of Guildford residents reported their country of birth as England

Health in Guildford

In 2021, 53.8% of Guildford residents described their health as "very good", increasing from 51.6% in 2011. Those describing their health as "good" fell from 34.1% to 33.0%. These are age-standardised proportions.

Age-standardised proportions are used throughout this section. They enable comparisons between populations over time and across geographies, as they account for differences in the population size and age structure.

The proportion of Guildford residents describing their health as "very bad" was 0.8% (similar to 2011), while those describing their health as "bad" was 2.6% (similar to 2011).

These data reflect people’s own opinions in describing their overall health on a five point scale, from very good to very bad.

Census 2021 was conducted during the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic. This may have influenced how people perceived and rated their health, and therefore may have affected how people chose to respond.

The percentage of people in very bad health in Guildford increased by 0.1 percentage points

National identity in Guildford

In 2021, 10.8% of Guildford residents did not identify with any national identity associated with the UK. This figure increased from 9.6% in 2011.

In 2021, just over 1 in 40 people (2.9%) identified with a UK and non-UK national identity, compared with 1.3% in 2011. The percentage of residents in Guildford that identified as "British only" increased from 18.4% to 56.3%.

The increase in the percentage of people who did not identify with any national identity associated with the UK was greater across the South East (1.6 percentage points, from 7.1% to 8.7%) than in Guildford (1.1 percentage points). Across England, the percentage increased by 1.7 percentage points, from 8.2% to 10.0%.

In Census 2021, “British” was moved to the top response option and this may have influenced how people described their national identity. For further information, please see our quality report.

The percentage of people who did not identify with at least one UK national identity in Guildford increased by 1.1 percentage points

Fewer couples without children

Of Guildford households, 18.0% included a couple but no children in 2021, down from 19.7% in 2011.

In 2021, just over one in five households (22.2%) included a couple with dependent children, compared with 22.9% in 2011. The percentage of single family households including a couple living with only non-dependent children increased from 5.9% to 6.4%.

The decrease in the percentage of households including a couple but no children was greater in Guildford (1.7 percentage points) than across the South East (1.4 percentage points, from 18.7% to 17.4%). Across England, the percentage fell by 0.9 percentage points, from 17.6% to 16.8%.

The percentage of households including a couple without children in Guildford decreased by 1.7 percentage points

More adults never married or in a civil partnership

Of Guildford residents aged 16 years and over, 39.3% said they had never been married or in a civil partnership in 2021, up from 35.2% in 2011.

In 2021, just under one in two people (46.5%) said they were married or in a registered civil partnership, compared with 49.6% in 2011. The percentage of adults in Guildford that had divorced or dissolved a civil partnership increased from 7.4% to 7.5%.

The increase in the percentage of people aged 16 years and over who had never been married or in a civil partnership was greater in Guildford (4.1 percentage points) than across the South East (2.9 percentage points, from 31.9% to 34.8%). Across England, the percentage increased by 3.3 percentage points, from 34.6% to 37.9%.

These figures include same-sex marriages and opposite-sex civil partnerships in 2021, neither of which were legally recognised in England and Wales in 2011. Same-sex marriages have been legally recognised in England and Wales since 2014 and opposite-sex civil partnerships have been recognised since 2019.

The percentage of adults who had never married or registered a civil partnership in Guildford increased by 4.1 percentage points

Disability in Guildford

In 2021, 4.8% of Guildford residents were identified as being disabled and limited a lot. This figure decreased from 5.7% in 2011. These are age-standardised proportions.

Age-standardised proportions are used throughout this section. They enable comparisons between populations over time and across geographies, as they account for differences in the population size and age structure.

In 2021, just under 1 in 11 people (8.9%) were identified as being disabled and limited a little, compared with 8.3% in 2011. The proportion of Guildford residents who were not disabled increased from 86.0% to 86.3%.

The decrease in the proportion of residents who were identified as being disabled and limited a lot in Guildford (0.9 percentage points) was similar to the decrease across the South East (1.0 percentage points, from 7.2% to 6.2%). Across England, the proportion fell by 1.6 percentage points, from 9.1% to 7.5%.

Census 2021 was undertaken during the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic. This may have influenced how people perceived their health status and activity limitations, and therefore may have affected how people chose to respond.

Caution should be taken when making comparisons between 2011 and 2021 because of changes in question wording and response options.

The percentage of people who were identified as being disabled and limited a lot in Guildford decreased by 0.9 percentage points

Ethnic groups in Guildford

In 2021, 6.7% of Guildford residents identified their ethnic group within the "Asian, Asian British or Asian Welsh" category, up from 4.8% in 2011. The 1.9 percentage-point change was the largest increase among high-level ethnic groups in this area.

Across the South East, the percentage of people from the "Asian, Asian British or Asian Welsh" ethnic group increased from 5.2% to 7.0%, while across England the percentage increased from 7.8% to 9.6%.

In 2021, 86.9% of people in Guildford identified their ethnic group within the "White" category (compared with 90.9% in 2011), while 3.1% identified their ethnic group within the "Mixed or Multiple" category (compared with 1.8% the previous decade).

The percentage of people who identified their ethnic group within the "Other" category ("Arab" or "Any other ethnic group") increased from 1.2% in 2011 to 1.9% in 2021.

There are many factors that may be contributing to the changing ethnic composition of England and Wales, such as differing patterns of ageing, fertility, mortality, and migration. Changes may also be caused by differences in the way individuals chose to self-identify between censuses.
